deep.reconstruction:
The page holds only a few jottings, unrelated to the prime-number computations on the preceding page.

(1) Top: a heavily struck-out expression, probably ∂p/∂x, followed by a colon.

(2) Next line: ∂r/∂x and a function φ applied to an argument. The argument is read as Δ but is quite possibly ρ. This looks like notation for a one-dimensional gas-dynamics problem: p is pressure, ρ is density, x is position, and r is possibly one of the Riemann-invariant-type quantities r, s from the 1860 paper on finite-amplitude plane air waves.

(3) Main line, after a struck-out symbol: dp/p = k dρ/ρ. This is the differential form of the adiabatic (Poisson) gas law. Integrating gives log p = k log ρ + const, i.e. p = C ρ^k (step supplied by me).

(4) Last line: φ(ρ) = k p/ρ. Read with the preceding line, this is dp/dρ = k p/ρ. Here φ denotes the derivative of pressure with respect to density, i.e. the squared speed of sound c² = k p/ρ (Laplace's adiabatic correction).

In the published 1860 paper Riemann writes p = φ(ρ) and uses φ'(ρ). On this page φ seems to stand for the derivative itself, or the prime has been omitted.

The page thus records the elementary ingredient needed for wave propagation in a polytropic gas: the local sound speed √(k p/ρ). This is the ingredient that enters the characteristic speeds u ± √φ'(ρ) in Riemann's theory.
errors: No mathematical error. The only issue is notational: if φ denotes pressure as a function of density (as in Riemann's 1860 paper), the last line should read φ'(ρ) = k p/ρ. As written, φ must be read as dp/dρ.
